solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Initially seen as crazy, keep bringing up the old musical instrument

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the seven words from seen to the

explanation.surface: Someone told to keep hauling up an antique instrument that seems mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' applies to every word from 'seen' to 'the': their first letters spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Renaissance brass instrument, the early form of the trombone, so an old instrument of music.

clue.text: Cancel fight

definitions.meaning: to call off or abandon a plan

explanation.definitionFit: To drop a plan is to cancel it, and a minor brawl is also called by this word.

clue.text: Touchy after legal proceedings seeing H and h as different?

definitions.text: seeing H and h as different?

indicators.note: after puts the word for touchy behind the word for legal proceedings

parts.note: a lawsuit is a case
touchy means easily offended, sensitive

explanation.surface: A litigant made thin-skinned by a court battle, oddly fussy about letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Touchy' as describing a person; it is a synonym placed after the legal word.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that treats capital and lower-case letters as distinct is described with this computing term.

clue.text: Splendid bachelor party

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: Someone praising a stag do as a splendid bachelor party.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned exclamation of approval: a fine show is called brave, meaning splendid.

clue.text: Nonsense about Henry's beat

indicators.note: about means the word for nonsense goes around the letter for Henry

parts.note: trash is rubbish, nonsense
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Talking nonsense about Henry's beat, as if he were a police officer or drummer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a thrashing is to beat them soundly, as a verb synonym.

clue.text: Caught by publicity about group

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an ad is a piece of publicity
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A news item: someone caught by publicity concerning a particular group.
explanation.definitionFit: A small trained core of people in a party or army is a group of activists or officers.

clue.text: Conservative with word of warning referring to type of lens

parts.note: cave, Latin for beware, was the schoolboy cry of warning

explanation.surface: A Tory issuing a warning about a particular kind of lens.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (pronounced 'kay-vee') was British public-school slang shouted to warn that a teacher was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenses are classed as curving inward or outward; the inward-curving kind is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Ten at heart of it, my cadet smiles, enigmatically

indicators.note: enigmatically suggests the letters of my cadet smiles are puzzlingly rearranged

explanation.surface: A proud parent: my cadet smiles enigmatically, like a military Mona Lisa.
explanation.definitionFit: Base-ten counting, the decimal arrangement, is a numbering scheme built on ten.

clue.text: This shows mistake was made — "maturer" is wrong

indicators.note: is wrong signals that the letters of maturer must be put right by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A correction slip announcing that the word maturer was printed in error.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the slip listed in a book's corrections page is itself made from a jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed correction notice lists an error in a book, so it shows that a mistake occurred.

clue.text: A race star turn, on the move, dining here?

indicators.note: on the move indicates the letters of a race star turn are shifted about

explanation.surface: A celebrity performer on a moving train, perhaps at a racecourse, wondering where to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage serving meals is where passengers eat while travelling, a dining carriage.

clue.text: Gain control over law-enforcing group, extremely sedulous

parts.note: a posse is a band summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law

indicators.note: extremely means only the outermost letters of sedulous are used

explanation.surface: A diligent sheriff's posse seizing control of a situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To take control of something is to take ownership or seize it, the verb's sense of acquiring.

clue.text: Let in a Duke with German

parts.note: mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A doorman allowing an aristocrat and a German companion entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow entry is to permit someone through the door, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Digress in law and err

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words law and err

explanation.surface: A lawyer's lament about straying from the point and making mistakes in law.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray from the subject when speaking is to drift or ramble off topic.

clue.text: Wife greeting Papa with favourite dog

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A wife greeting her father along with the family's beloved dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim, fast greyhound-like breed bred for racing, so a kind of dog.

clue.text: Competitor in from France managed to get into Tourist Trophy

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: to get into says the verb for managed goes inside the race initials

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorbike races
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A French rider managing to get a place in the Isle of Man TT race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tourist Trophy (TT) is a famous motorcycle road race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has entered a race or contest is a participant, a competitor.

clue.text: After sleep, left in the morning uproar

indicators.note: after places the morning and left pieces behind the word for sleep

parts.note: bed stands for sleep, as in going to bed
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: Waking and departing in the morning to find chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: BED for sleep is loose, as in 'time for bed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after a notorious London asylum, the word means chaotic noise and confusion, an uproar.

clue.text: Famous person's stage of journey coming to close

parts.note: a leg is one stage of a journey
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A celebrity's tour reaching its final leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay; 'coming to' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated figure renowned in a field is called by this word, as in a sporting great.

clue.text: Wild, hit out regularly? Silly

indicators.note: regularly asks for every second letter of wild, hit out

explanation.surface: Someone lashing out wildly, and being called silly for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' is a noun here, as in 'you silly!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a fool affectionately uses the noun form, a dimwit or nitwit.

clue.text: He tries tips from Erasmus, say, with indication of hesitation

indicators.note: tips from means the two ends of Erasmus are used

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: A scholar's hesitant attempt to quote Erasmus.
explanation.walkthrough: Erasmus, the great essayist, makes a neat surface for someone who tries.
explanation.definitionFit: One who attempts or tests something is a trier; this old noun comes from the verb assay.

clue.text: Tantrum noticed by sound of it

indicators.note: by sound of it says the word for noticed is said aloud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: noticed means seen

explanation.surface: Spotting a child's tantrum by the noise it makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a fuss in public, an angry outburst or display of temper, as in don't make a fuss.

clue.text: Second showing somewhat nearer university

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A second showing of a film somewhere close to a university campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second showing' reads as one phrase, but only 'Second' defines; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat broadcast of a programme is a second airing, so a second showing.

clue.text: Government not in control of this soldier faction meeting other ranks

definitions.text: Government not in control of this

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
a sect is a faction
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks

explanation.surface: A soldiers' faction meeting enlisted men, a political plot in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Businesses owned privately rather than by the state make up the part of the economy outside government.

clue.text: Stealing article, flees town at first

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of flees and of town

explanation.surface: A thief grabs an item and flees the town in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking what belongs to someone else is a crime of stealing, the noun for robbery.

clue.text: That will never happen, road men at work

indicators.note: at work signals that the letters of road men are busy being rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic saying the road crew will never actually be seen working.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive retort meaning your hope is fantasy: keep wishing, it won't happen.
